PullRequest.Title: Agents - Move Commit Action to Changes Toolbar
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request relocates the Commit action to the Changes header while maintaining pull-request actions in the title bar. The changes ensure that the UI behavior is consistent and that no medium or high-severity issues remain.

Key changes include:

- **File Modifications**: Adjustments made in six files, including `changesActions.ts`, `changesView.ts`, and `agentHostChangesetOperationService.ts`.
- **Behavior Consistency**: Ensured that the selected changeset behavior and operation filtering across branches are correctly implemented.
- **Testing**: All modified files were reviewed, and focused tests passed successfully, confirming that the changes do not introduce any new issues.
- **Quality Assurance**: Completed type checking, linting, and validation checks to ensure code quality.

No additional code changes were necessary as the existing patterns were adhered to throughout the modifications.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore an existing session or switch the selected Changes changeset
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The AfterRestored contribution synchronously reads the active session, selected changeset, and advertised operations, filters for the Commit operation, and registers at most one command/menu item. Changeset loading can delay the action appearing, but no filesystem, subprocess, IPC, database, or network work is initiated by the new autorun.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The selected changeset catalogue and its operation list. Selection remains the existing O(changesets) projection, while the added branch scans the selected operation list and retains at most one Commit action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single observable autorun executes synchronously; dependency changes dispose the prior registration before registering the replacement. There is no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active changeset projection is a cached derived observable and preserves the last equivalent changeset while loading. Cold state registers no action until data arrives; warm updates reuse the cached projection but replace the bounded action registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete autorun and derived-observable implementations show only in-memory filtering plus command/menu registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Operation-list sizes and update rates vary by provider, but the host operation set is small and only one action survives the filter.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing sessions now cause bounded registration work on selection or operation-status changes, but there is no scaling expensive boundary or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update Commit and pull-request controls in the Changes editor and title bar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar construction creates the existing ChangesWorkbenchButtonBarWidget, filters operations through a set membership check, and updates the existing button bar. The new Commit action renders one icon/label in the header. This is synchronous UI work but contains no geometry reads, forced layout, or collection-wide reconstruction beyond the already-observed small operation list.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of advertised changeset operations and number of active toolbar instances. The diff adds one O(1) exclusion check per operation and a bounded empty Set per widget construction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and observable reactions run serially on the UI thread; no async work is launched until a user invokes an action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm operation updates flow through existing derived observables and button-bar update logic. The exclusion sets are immutable for widget lifetime; no cache misses or negative-cache retries are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed constructors and filters were traced through ChangesActionsBar and ChangesWorkbenchButtonBarWidget.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu update frequency depends on provider status events, but each update is bounded by the small advertised operation set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added allocations and filtering are bounded and do not create forced layout, frame-frequency work, or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute and publish operations after Git or GitHub state changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentHostChangesetOperationService already recomputes operations for subscribed changesets and emits one ChangesetOperationsChanged envelope per changeset. The changed scope filter now includes pull-request descriptors for Uncommitted changesets, adding constant payload data but no additional recomputation pass or envelope.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing ChangesetOperationsChanged state envelope to subscribed clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing envelope per effective subscribed changeset during an operation recomputation; the diff adds up to the already-computed pull-request descriptors to an Uncommitted changeset's array but adds no envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Uncommitted changeset envelope was emitted with pull-request operations filtered out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The envelope must reach the renderer before the newly available controls update, but its call count and scheduling are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective subscribed changesets after owner/subscription resolution, typically branch and uncommitted changesets per scoped folder/chat owner. Added work is constant per affected Uncommitted envelope, not per file change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Owners and changesets are traversed synchronously and envelopes are dispatched serially; the diff adds no Promise fan-out or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Git and GitHub state are read from existing services/state; no new reads, cache keys, misses, or invalidation behavior are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed filter, operation provider's fixed-size output, subscription resolution, and dispatch path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Multi-root sessions can have multiple owners, but the operation publication loop and envelope cardinality predate this change; only a small fixed descriptor payload changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Serialization bytes increase by a bounded constant on existing envelopes without new IPC calls or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Commit or Create Pull Request from the relocated/newly available control
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user click invokes the selected changeset operation through one agent-host request, then the existing handler performs its Git and GitHub work. The UI awaits that explicit operation, but no automatic invocation is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one invokeChangesetOperation request to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per user invocation; in-flight host operations remain coalesced/serialized by operation key and lane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Commit and pull-request controls already invoked the same changeset RPC from their prior locations; the diff changes control placement and allows the PR workflow while Uncommitted is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user-requested operation waits for this request and handler completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing bounded Git workflow for PR preparation/creation, including reading state and committing/pushing when required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing workflow per explicit PR invocation, serialized for the same changeset and operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same workflow required invoking the PR action from a Branch changeset rather than while Uncommitted was selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Git work is on the explicit Create PR critical path, unchanged by the toolbar relocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use existing GitHub/Copilot services to read merge capabilities, generate metadata, push, and create or reuse a pull request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded existing sequence per explicit PR workflow; the diff does not add parallel requests or repeat the handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same network workflow was available from the Branch changeset; the changed scope makes the same single workflow reachable from Uncommitted without adding calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls determine explicit PR preparation/creation latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User invocations, not file count or render frequency. Uncommitted file count can affect the unchanged Git handler, but the diff does not increase handler frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The UI sends one request per click. The host coalesces identical in-flight requests and serializes each changeset/operation lane; no new aggregate concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Operation descriptors and state use existing observables; Git/GitHub service caching is unchanged. There is no new retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: UI invocation, protocol request, lane coalescing, and existing PR handler boundaries were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual Git and network duration depends on repository and connectivity, but the before/after invocation count is one for the same user workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes action reachability and placement but does not add automatic expensive work, extra requests, or increased concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and every diff hunk for the performance focus. Traced startup/session restore, observable/menu updates, toolbar rendering, operation publication, and explicit operation invocation through IPC, Git, and network boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
